title: Pointer and value receivers: the choice that changes behaviour

videos.script: Lesson 25 gave types their methods. A receiver can be written two ways, and this lesson is about the asterisk that separates them. {{copy}} A counter with two methods, both adding one. One is written with a value receiver, and the count stays at zero. The other takes a pointer, and the count goes up. Nothing else in the two methods differs. {{refused}} Then the places where Go will not take the address for you. A map element. A literal. The compiler refuses both, and its message says why. {{print}} Then a change of behaviour with no error at all. A String method on a pointer, and fmt prints the raw struct instead of your format. The reason is a rule called the method set. It also decides which interfaces a type satisfies. {{choose}} Last, how to choose. You will read the standard library's own answers, in time and in strings. By the end, you can look at a type and say which receiver its methods want.
